main_text.p: Epicurus contrá videtur judiciu veri sensib. attribuisse λέγει ἓν ὁ Ἐπίκουρος, ληπτὴ τὰ ἀληθέα ἕνια αὐδύσεις, ἡ προλήψεις, ἡ τὰ πάθη: ait siquidem Epicurus judicia veritatis esse sensus, & anticipationes, & affectiones. At Aristoteles utrūq; & sensus & 5 intellectus judiciū cōplexus est, intellectumq; sensui longissimé præposuit: Nā tametsi notiones intellectus deducit á sensibus & sensiliū inductione rerū, & animadversione atq; experientia, ut colligit: statuit tn intellectu judiciū ratione visis reb. adjūcta, sensu certius: quantoq; remotiō á sensu notionis genus est, tátó αἰτιωτέρον, ἀρχικώτερον, ἐπιστημονικώτερον, καὶ τῇ φύσει πρότερον, καὶ γνωριμώτερον: causse & principio & scientiæ vicinius, & naturâ prius ac notius: ut jam dictū est, 5 sic sane notionum earum judicium præstantius & excellentius.
main_text.head: Cap. III. De Enuntiato simplici.
main_text.p: ENuntiatum, est simplex aut cōpositum. Simplex, est quo sententia simplex enuntiatur: itaq; vno verbo continetur, quo affirmato affirmatur, negato negatur: ut, ignis urit, ignis est calidus, ignis non est aqua: hic (ignis) est antecedens: (urit) consequens. Atq; hic prima est inventarū rerum dispositio, caussæ cum effecto, ut in primo exemplo: subjecti cum adjuncto, ut in secundo: dissentanei cū dissentaneo, ut in tertio: quomodo argumentū quodlibet enun tiari

page.notes: Marginal numerals 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 are line numbers; 5 and 5 (second) are shown above as printed "5" and "5I"; the printed margin numerals are reproduced as they appear. Greek passages are transcribed approximately from a small, damaged scan and may contain errors. Some words are doubtful: "tn" for "tamen"/"tñ" and "sensiliū" may be misprints; catchword "tiari" at the foot of the column is a running continuation of the word "enuntiatur".
